newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blast rocks Algerian garrison town - residents.
newsitem.headline: Blast rocks Algerian garrison town - residents.

text.p: A powerful bomb rocked a market in the centre of the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, on Wednesday morning, residents said.
"The blast occurred in a market in central Blida but we do not know what caused it," one resident said by telephone from the city.
Blida is known as a Moslem guerrilla stronghold and a "corridor" for rebels to reach their hideouts in surrounding mountains.
The blast in Blida, site of the army headquarters, came one day after two car bomb explosions killed at least 12 and wounded scores in Algiers.

The two bombs that rocked central Algiers in less than five hours on Tuesday brought the toll since the start of the Moslem holy month of Ramadan on January 10 to at least 150 and 170 wounded, Algerian newspapers said.

No one has claimed responsibility but political analysts believe the bombs are a message to President Liamine Zeroual that the Islamic fundamentalists remain a formidable force despite repeated claims by the government to have crushed them.
Algiers residents reported leaflets posted in the Casbah said there would be 50 bombs during Ramadan. The Armed Islamic Group (GIA) had warned it would increase attacks during Ramadan.
Residents said military officers defused two booby-trapped cars set to explode in Algiers streets on Tuesday. More than 15 other bombs had been defused in the past three weeks, they said.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election that radical Islamists were poised to win.
